blind_classification.method: A fresh agent instance, with no access to team_category above or to this project's conversation history, was given only poem/base_text/variant/part_of_speech plus the paper's own Level 1 and Level 2 taxonomy definitions (quoted verbatim), and asked to classify each pair.

results.reason: "World" expands the scope of "souls" from personal to cosmic magnitude, and nothing in the poem forces a choice among the three noun variants.
"selves" is essentially synonymous with "souls" (both denote the inner person), offered alongside other options with no textual basis to prefer it.
"Sun" turns the felt loss of a "soul" into a cosmic/vital image, heightening rather than replacing the sense of loss.
"Life" downgrades the intensified positive state named by "Bliss" to mere neutral existence, an implicit opposition in value/tone.
"dare" locates agency in the self while "allowed" relocates it to external permission, an opposition in the source of agency.
"click" and "start" both denote a brief, sudden occurrence, so click just restates the idea in more mechanical/sensory terms.
"Sepulchre" and "Wilderness" intensify the abstract "Bankruptcy" into vivid images of death and desolation.
"Noon" pushes "Sun" to its most extreme, fullest point in the daily cycle, magnifying rather than merely restating it.
"Meridian" names the same "peak point" idea as "Midsummer," just transposed from seasonal to diurnal register.
In the noon-to-night progression, "Night" reverses the light/vitality connoted by the surrounding "time" imagery.
"tangible" and "positive" both raise the epistemic certainty of "plausible" from merely believable to verified/concrete.
"true" and "real" are near-synonyms describing authenticity, so the variant restates rather than shifts the base meaning.
"Truth" restates the concept named by "Real" (authenticity/actuality) rather than opposing or amplifying it.
"been one" reads as a successive completion continuing "but been" rather than a true substitute reading.
"bleak" injects a negative affective charge that opposes the neutral/persistent sense of "but been," echoing the poem's bliss/bleak tension.
"rectified" implies restoring wholeness/correctness while "qualified" implies limitation or partial condition, opposing senses of completeness.
